question: trace the dispatcher 0x5bba800's 0x4000-exit body at 0x5bbb030..0x5bbb62a and name its operation: whether it is the same ChaCha block function at a wider vector form, and how its counter/output contract compares to the F2 (SSSE3) body's

trace.frame: sub rsp,0x68 at entry, add rsp,0x68 before ret (the SSSE3 form's frame is 0x38)

input.bytes_read: 0x00..0x30 of the record (three 16-byte rows); bytes 0x30.. of the record are never read
input.counter: the 64-bit word at [rdi+0x20]; variants +0/+1/+2/+3 built at 0x5bbb041, 0x5bbb05a, 0x5bbb06e -- each variant row is the loaded counter/nonce row with its first two dwords replaced by the variant counter (vpinsrd $0 with the lea result's low dword, vpinsrd $1 with its shr 0x20 high dword), one row per block

round_count_gate.parameter: esi = iterations of the round loop; each iteration runs two double rounds (four ChaCha rounds)

post_loop_feed_forward.note: the four constant rows receive the sigma add here; every other row's feed-forward add happens in the shared epilogue from the entry-saved originals

zero_round_path.note: with esi == 0 no round runs: the constant rows are loaded with 2*sigma per word (the feed-forward sum precomputed) and the other rows are doubled by the epilogue adds, so the output is exactly initial + initial

encoding.note: every vector instruction is VEX-encoded in three-operand non-destructive form, and every vector register operand is an xmm register; no ymm operand occurs anywhere in the body

same: input: bytes 0x00..0x30 of the record at rdi (three 16-byte rows); the counter is the 64-bit word at [rdi+0x20], with +0/+1/+2/+3 variant rows, one per block
round-count contract: esi counts round-loop iterations, each running two double rounds; esi == 0 takes the doubled-sigma path and the output is exactly initial + initial
round loop: the rotation census is identical (32 paddd, 32 pxor, 16 pshufb, rotations 16/12/8/7 at 8 each, pshufd lane rotations 0x39/0x4e/0x93 at 8/8/4)

constants: the same four .rodata references (sigma 0x4519c0, doubled sigma 0x456c50, rotate-by-8 mask 0x4531c0, swap mask 0x452ec0) with the same reference pattern (sigma twice, rotate-by-8 mask twice, swap mask once, doubled sigma once on the zero-round path)
feed-forward: four sigma adds after the loop and 12 adds in the shared epilogue

counter/output contract: the counter word at [rdi+0x20] is stored back advanced by 4, and 256 bytes -- four 64-byte ChaCha blocks for counters c, c+1, c+2, c+3 -- are stored to rdx in 16 vector stores; no return value
structure: no calls, exactly three branches, all internal, and a single ret
different: encoding: VEX (vpaddd/vpxor/vpshufb/vmovdqa, three-operand non-destructive) against the F2 body's legacy SSE encoding -- vector width is 128-bit xmm in both, with no ymm operand in either body, so the four-block parallelism is unchanged: this is not a wider-vector form
counter construction: vpinsrd low/high pairs against movd/shr plus shuffle/or merging
size: 1,530 bytes / 301 instructions against 1,758 bytes / 340 instructions; the round loop is 189 instructions against 217
a vzeroupper at 0x5bbb622 before ret, which the legacy-SSE form does not emit

exit_4000.shape: add rsp,0xa8; pop rbx; pop r14; pop r15; pop rbp; jmp -- the dispatcher's frame is fully unwound before the jump, so the 0x4000-exit body is entered with the caller's own arguments (rdi, esi, rdx) and its ret returns straight to the dispatcher's caller

direct_transfers.note: every E8/E9 byte hit in .text was validated against its containing FDE's disassembly; the sole direct transfer to the traced body is the dispatcher's 0x4000 exit jump at 0x5bbafc5, and there is no call

operation.name: ChaCha block function (AVX / VEX-encoded form): four blocks in parallel with feed-forward, the state's 64-bit counter advanced by 4
operation.contract: input rdi = a state record of which bytes 0x00..0x30 are read (key rows at +0x00/+0x10 and the counter/nonce row at +0x20, whose first 64-bit word is the counter); esi = round-loop iterations (two double rounds each); output rdx receives 256 bytes -- four 64-byte ChaCha blocks for counters c, c+1, c+2, c+3, each the sum of its worked state and its initial state -- and the counter word at [rdi+0x20] is stored back advanced by 4; no return value.  The contract is identical to the SSSE3 form at 0x5bba120 in every observable respect
evidence: the body's round constants are the ChaCha constants: the 16-byte ASCII string "expand 32-byte k" at 0x4519c0 (the sigma row) and, for the zero-round path, its exact double at 0x456c50 (per-word 2*sigma), referenced from the same pattern of sites as in the F2 body

the round loop is the ChaCha quarter-round network on 32-bit words, with a rotation census identical to the SSSE3 form's: vpaddd/vpxor with rotations 16 (vpshuflw/vpshufhw 0xb1 word swaps), 12 (vpsrld 0x14 / vpslld 0xc), 8 (vpshufb through the byte-rotation mask at 0x4531c0) and 7 (vpsrld 0x19 / vpslld 0x7), with vpshufd 0x39/0x4e/0x93 lane rotations for the diagonal rounds and a second byte mask at 0x452ec0
the entry builds four counter rows from the 64-bit counter at [rdi+0x20] (+0/+1/+2/+3) -- four blocks worked in lockstep, one counter step apart, in transposed form

the epilogue is the ChaCha feed-forward: worked rows are added to the entry-saved initial rows (the constant rows receive their sigma add just after the loop) and stored as 16 vector stores covering 256 bytes, and the counter row is stored back at [rdi+0x20] with the counter advanced by 4

the wider-vector hypothesis fails on the operands: every vector instruction is VEX-encoded, but every vector register operand is xmm (128-bit) and no ymm operand occurs anywhere in the 301 instructions -- the form differs from the SSSE3 form in encoding only, not in width or parallelism
